notes: ScienceDirect refused. The source is NREL's copy of the published article (Elsevier layout, available online 31 July 2024), which gives full names; Oxford's ORA record agrees, with initials. Comparators were not requested for this item, but its content bears on the manuscript: 32 two-cell tests of P42A and LG M50 21700 cells in series and parallel, cans in direct contact in a stacking holder, trigger nailed near its centre. 18 of 32 (56%) propagated; propagation needed the neighbour at about 150 C; the fastest time to propagation was 123 s (abstract, Table 1); group means were about 212 s (M50 parallel) and 220 s (M50 series) in the tables. The reader tool reported that the conclusion quotes 123 s to 467 s while the slowest tabulated value is 464 s; check this before quoting the range.

Inverted, that is a contact resistance of about 1.1e-3 m2 K W-1, by my arithmetic. The authors expect a higher conductance in cells with electrolyte.
